deliberation: Attribution is not identity: a proxy act remains a machine act even under a human-created delegation. It cannot satisfy a rule requiring direct substantive authenticated human action. Motion A may support already-authorized nondiscretionary execution, but Motion B changes current staffing, office-power, and autonomous-permission rules and conflicts with GI-STEWARD-0002 until Article XI action. The operative primitives and authority equation remain underdefined, so committee rework is required before Human Steward disposition.
discharged_obligations: Exposed the primitive identities, acts, authority sources, assumptions, and constitutional invariants.
Separated task-class authority, exact-task authorization, proxy execution, and human action.
findings: A proxy act cannot manufacture human review, approval, presence, signature, or judgment.
Delegable authority must originate in effective policy and may only narrow the principal's authority.
Routine and control-plane require normative closed classification and dependency closure.
Reversible and compensable are distinct authority and risk classes.
Motion B requires a complete Article XI package.
amendments: Define qualifying human acts and attributed proxy acts positively and separately.
Use an intersection-based non-amplification authority rule.
Define explicit delegator roles, closed task classes, exact instance scope, expiry, revocation, holds, and evidence.
Keep identity, credentials, proxy-policy activation, and permission changes control-plane.
Return a complete committee package for renewed unanimous Council review and separate Human Steward disposition.
residual_uncertainty: No task inventory, classifier, delegation schema, credential design, or migration rule exists.
Agent-office infrastructure and session independence are unresolved.
